h1: Opioid Addiction Treatment in Los Angeles
sub: Medication and therapy for opioid addiction at our Westwood center, and you sleep at home every night. Our [addiction treatment center in Los Angeles](/) treats everything from pain pills to fentanyl.

hero.alt: A private therapy room at Golden State Rehab with a sofa and an armchair
hero.caption: One-on-one sessions happen in here

sections.q: What does opioid addiction treatment involve?
sections.a: Opioid addiction changes the brain's reward system, whether it started with a pain prescription or with heroin from the street. Stopping without help gets very hard. We treat it with medication like buprenorphine (Suboxone) plus therapy, in a full-day program (PHP) or in 3-hour sessions a few days a week (IOP).
sections.note: All of it happens at our center on Westwood Blvd, a few minutes from the 405 and the 10.

items.d: Cognitive behavioral therapy. You work on the triggers and thought patterns behind your use, and make a plan for cravings and high-risk moments.
Peer support and accountability from people who know what opioid recovery takes.
Small rewards for clean tests and for showing up. It's one of the most effective behavorial tools for opioid addiction.
Opioid addiction often comes with trauma or PTSD. We treat both together, as part of the same plan.

sections.q: Do I need detox before I start Suboxone?
sections.a: Usually not. Buprenorphine (Suboxone) relieves withdrawal itself, so many people start it early in outpatient care. If you've been using [fentanyl](/treatments/fentanyl), the start takes more care, because fentanyl stays in the body longer. Your free assessment tells us what's safe for you.
sections.note: If detox is the safer first step for you, we set it up with a trusted detox provider and hold your spot.

items.d: By phone or in person. We go over what you've been using and for how long.
Our medical team picks a safe way to begin buprenorphine, with extra care if fentanyl is involved.
Buprenorphine eases withdrawal and cravings, so your head is clear enough for therapy.
You start PHP or IOP here in Westwood and go home at night.

sections.q: Should I take Suboxone or Vivitrol?
sections.a: Our medical team helps you choose. Buprenorphine (Suboxone) can start early and eases withdrawal while you settle into treatment. Naltrexone (Vivitrol) is a non-opioid option for people who have already finished detox and want nothing opioid in their system.

rows: Blocks the effect of other opioids
You can work and live your normal day on it
Blocks opioid receptors, so using brings no reward

sections.q: Isn't Suboxone just trading one drug for another?
sections.a: No. Buprenorphine is medicine for a medical condition. At a steady prescribed dose it doesn't make you high. It quiets withdrawal and cravings so therapy has room to work. SAMHSA and the American Society of Addiction Medicine both support its use.

items: Medications like buprenorphine lower the risk of dying from an overdose.
People on MAT (medication-assisted treatment) are more likely to stay in treatment.
People on MAT tend to do better at work and at home.
Some programs still discourage MAT. Here it's part of the plan.

sections.q: Will my insurance pay for opioid treatment?
sections.a: It depends on your plan. We work with most major PPO plans, and many plans may cover medication and therapy for opioid addiction. We check your benefits for free, usually within the hour, so you can decide with the facts in hand.
sections.note: Under federal parity law and California's SB 855, health plans have to cover medically necessary addiction care.

sections.q: Will my boss find out I'm on Suboxone?
sections.a: Not from us. HIPAA and 42 CFR Part 2, a federal privacy law written for addiction treatment, protect your records, and we never contact your employer. Most of our clients keep working. [IOP](/programs/iop) has morning and evening tracks, and many sessions can happen by telehealth.
sections.note: If you do need time off, federal FMLA and California's CFRA usually protect your job, and the leave request doesn't have to say why.

sections.q: I just finished detox. What do I do now?
sections.a: Call us for a free assessment. Most people start within days of their first call, so the support doesn't stop when detox ends. If you've finished withdrawal and want a non-opioid medication, naltrexone (Vivitrol) is one way to protect the progress you made.
